sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Unit assessment. Work alone, show your steps, and check your work before you finish.

items.prompt: In a study, P(passes | attended the workshop) is higher than P(passes) overall. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
Attendance and passing are associated, though this alone does not show that the workshop caused the improvement.

items.prompt: A box holds 9 items, of which 6 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 2/20 and P(B) = 14/20, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 6/20, P(B) = 7/20, and P(A and B) = 4/20, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, P(has the condition | tested positive) is much smaller than P(tested positive | has the condition). What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two events are mutually exclusive.
The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
The two conditional probabilities condition on different events, so they need not be close; a rare condition makes the first much smaller.

items.prompt: A box holds 9 items, of which 5 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 57/100 and P(B) = 59/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 27/100, P(B) = 8/100, and P(A and B) = 4/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
In a study, the probability of a delay is the same whether or not it is raining. What is the correct interpretation?
choices: The two conditional probabilities are equal, so the order of conditioning never matters.
Delay and rain are independent, because conditioning on rain does not change the probability of a delay.
The relationship proves that one event causes the other.
The two events are mutually exclusive.

items.prompt: A box holds 20 items, of which 3 are defective. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both are defective, in lowest terms.
Given P(A and B) = 1/100 and P(B) = 7/100, find P(A | B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Given P(A) = 25/100, P(B) = 10/100, and P(A and B) = 1/100, find P(A or B) in lowest terms.
